meta.subtitle: Margins and cash flow are rising, but at 70.4x trailing earnings and near the 52-week high the shares already price in much of it

analystSentiment.commentary:
Red Violet's second quarter of 2026 was strong on every line the MD&A reports: revenue, gross margin, net income and operating cash flow all rose faster than in the year-ago quarter. The business is growing at roughly 20% a year and converting a rising share of revenue into cash.

The share price has already moved to reflect that. At $79.55 on October 2, 2026 the stock sits close to its 52-week high of $81.80 and far above the low of $33.40. It trades at 70.4x trailing earnings, and the consensus target of $84.50 implies only +6.2% from here.

The August 2026 equity offering changes the story from here: the company now holds far more cash than its operations need, and management has named potential strategic acquisitions as one use. How well that cash is deployed matters more to the next year than the core business does.

We rate RDVT HOLD with a $72–$90 target range. We like the business; we do not find the price attractive enough to buy.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Red Violet, Inc. is an analytics and information solutions company that delivers identity intelligence in the United States. Its cloud-native platform, CORE, combines public records, proprietary and publicly-available data with machine learning to identify and locate people, businesses, assets and their relationships.

The company markets its solutions mainly through two brands. IDI's flagship product, idiCORE, is an investigative tool used for due diligence, identity authentication, fraud prevention, regulatory compliance and debt recovery by financial services firms, insurers, law enforcement, law firms, collections agencies and others. FOREWARN is an app-based solution currently tailored for the real estate industry, giving agents information about a consumer before a face-to-face meeting.

Red Violet reports a single segment, earns substantially all of its revenue from licensing its solutions, and is headquartered in Boca Raton, Florida.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body: The business case is good: steady double-digit growth, widening margins, no debt and strong cash conversion. The valuation case is weaker. At the current price the shares already discount most of the outcome we think likely, so our probability-weighted fair value sits close to the current price (see Valuation). We would need either a lower entry price or evidence that the offering proceeds are being deployed into value-creating acquisitions to move to BUY.

catalysts: How management deploys the proceeds of the August 2026 equity offering, including any acquisition.
Third-quarter 2026 results and whether the margin gains of the second quarter hold.
Continued customer and user growth at IDI and FOREWARN.
Use of the remaining authorization under the Stock Repurchase Program.
risks: A high multiple that leaves little room for any slowdown in growth.
A data breach or privacy incident at a company that stores sensitive consumer information.
An acquisition that overpays or proves hard to integrate.
Dilution from new share issuance if the proceeds earn a low return.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY25 revenue was $90.3M, up {+20.0%+}, after growth of 24.9% in FY24 and 12.9% in FY23. Operating margin has risen every year in the series, from -3.0% in FY21 to 14.6% in FY25. FY25 net income was $13.2M, or $0.91 per diluted share.

The second quarter of 2026 extended the trend. Revenue rose 23% to $26.7 million, gross margin increased to 76% from 72%, and net income rose 85% to $5.0 million, or $0.34 per diluted share. Adjusted EBITDA was $11.2 million, a 42% margin against 35% a year earlier.

The counter-case is in the definitions. Adjusted EBITDA excludes share-based compensation, depreciation and amortization, and the GAAP net income margin for the quarter was 19%. Investors paying for the adjusted figures should keep the GAAP margin in view, since that is what the trailing P/E is built on.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary:
Red Violet carries no debt in any year from FY22 to FY25 in our data. Cash and cash equivalents were $50.0 million at June 30, 2026, and the trailing current ratio is 10.88.

The August 2026 offering of 1,916,667 shares brought net proceeds of approximately $109.0 million, which comes after the quarter end and so is not in the June balance. The balance sheet is now far larger than the business needs to run. That removes any financing risk, but cash held on the balance sheet earns little, so the return on equity depends on how the proceeds are used.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow was $28.8M in FY25, a 31.9% FCF margin against 19.7% in FY21. Capital expenditure was only -$563,000 in FY25, so almost all operating cash flow becomes free cash flow. In the second quarter of 2026, net cash provided by operating activities rose to $10.6 million.

The business funds itself comfortably. The issue is price: at the current market value the trailing FCF yield is 2.6%, which gives a holder little cash return while waiting for growth to compound.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $79.55 RDVT trades at 70.4x trailing earnings, 47.9x NTM earnings, 12.9x trailing sales and 66.0x trailing EV/EBITDA. The snapshot's forward P/E on FY27E is ~45.2x; we use the NTM figure as the main forward measure.

The Street is uniformly positive but sees little upside: all 4 covering analysts rate Buy, yet the consensus target is $84.50 with a median of $87.50 and a range of $73.00–$90.00. The top of that range is only modestly above today's price.

Consensus also expects EPS to grow much more slowly than revenue: $1.66 for FY26E and $1.76 for FY27E, against revenue of $106.7M and $120.8M. The data we hold does not explain that gap, and it makes the forward multiple harder to justify on earnings alone.

We have no peer multiples to compare against, so we judge the price against the growth rate and the cash yield instead.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Revenue growth holds near recent rates, margins keep widening, and the offering proceeds fund an acquisition the market sees as accretive. The shares rise above the top of the Street target range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: The company delivers consensus revenue and earnings, the cash is deployed slowly, and the multiple holds roughly where it is. The shares end near the Street consensus target.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Growth slows, a privacy or data-security problem damages customer trust, or an acquisition disappoints. The multiple compresses sharply toward the levels the stock traded at earlier in its 52-week range.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries the most weight because it needs only consensus delivery at an unchanged multiple. Bear carries more weight than Bull because the starting multiple is high: a modest disappointment would cost more than a modest beat would add.

The result is a weighted fair value of $78, an expected upside of -1.4% and a bear-case downside of -30.9%. That falls short of our BUY threshold, and the downside is far larger than the expected return.

Our $72–$90 target range brackets Base.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Red Violet reports a single segment and does not break out revenue by brand. The MD&A gives the operating measures instead: as of June 30, 2026 IDI had 10,869 billable customers against 9,549 a year earlier, and FOREWARN had 443,173 users against 346,671. In the three months ended June 30, 2026, 77% of revenue came from customers with pricing contracts and 23% from transactional customers. Pricing contracts are generally annual or longer with auto renewal, which makes most revenue recurring.

moatFactors.name: Data assets and platform
moatFactors.body: CORE combines public records, proprietary and publicly-available data with machine learning built into the platform. Assembling and maintaining such datasets takes time and money, which deters small entrants. The 10-K warns that the data and analytics sector changes rapidly and that competitors may introduce products that make existing ones obsolete.

moatFactors.name: Workflow embedding
moatFactors.body: The company's land-and-expand model starts with a trial and grows as customers add use cases across departments and become reliant on the solutions in their daily workflow. Contracted revenue with auto renewal (see Segments) supports retention. The limit is that customers can still move to another data provider at renewal.

moatFactors.name: FOREWARN distribution
moatFactors.body: 660 REALTOR Associations are now contracted to use FOREWARN, which gives the product a distribution channel into the real estate industry that a new entrant would need years to build. It also ties FOREWARN's growth to a single industry.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. Rising margins and contracted, renewing revenue are consistent with real customer reliance. We stop short of wide because the company is small, its data advantage depends on continued investment in a fast-changing sector, and a single serious security incident could undo customer trust quickly. The moat holds if CORE keeps pace with technology change and the company avoids a breach.

points: Consensus expects FY26E revenue of ~$106.7M, up 18%, a slight slowdown from FY25. That is a reasonable bar given the second-quarter pace, but it is the bar the current price already assumes.
Customer additions remain steady: IDI added 447 customers and FOREWARN added 25,493 users in the second quarter. Continued additions at that pace support the land-and-expand model described in Moat.

Acquisitions are the new swing factor. Management intends to use the offering proceeds for working capital and general corporate purposes, including potential strategic acquisitions. A well-priced deal could add growth; an expensive one would dilute returns on a much larger equity base.
In our view, FOREWARN's reach beyond real estate is an open question: the MD&A describes it as currently tailored for that industry, so any broadening would be new growth the numbers do not yet show.

management.leadership: No proxy statement was captured for this report, so we do not name or comment on individual executives. The MD&A describes the operating approach: an inside sales team, a strategic sales team for major accounts, and distributors, resellers and strategic partners, with management continuing to build out the sales organization. The steady improvement in margins over five years is the main evidence of execution available to us.
management.capitalAllocation:
Red Violet pays no dividend. Year to date through June 30, 2026 it purchased 74,500 shares at an average price of $41.87 under its Stock Repurchase Program, with $15.5 million remaining on the authorization.

In August 2026 it then sold new shares in the public offering. Buying stock at the lower prices earlier in 2026 and issuing it after the share price rose is sound sequencing. The larger test is still ahead: the company now has to earn an adequate return on the new cash, and the filing names acquisitions as one possible use without identifying any target.
management.governance: No proxy statement was captured for this report, so we cannot assess board composition and independence, executive pay, insider ownership or related-party dealings. We make no governance claims beyond that gap, and readers should consult the company's latest proxy before relying on this section.

idiosyncratic: Data security: the 10-K says the company aggregates, stores and processes a large amount of sensitive consumer information, and that a breach could cause a material loss of business, legal liability or reputational harm. It also notes that insurance may not cover the full cost.

Privacy regulation: the 10-K warns that concerns about the collection, use and sharing of personal information, and compliance with state and federal data privacy laws, could raise costs or restrict the business.
Technology change: the 10-K says success depends on developing new products in a timely manner and that competitors' products could make existing ones obsolete.
Capital deployment: in our view, the offering proceeds raise the risk of an overpriced or poorly integrated acquisition, and new shares dilute existing holders if the cash earns a low return.
Valuation: at the multiples set out in Valuation, a modest slowdown in growth could cause a sharp fall in the share price even if the business keeps growing.
risks.systemic: FOREWARN is tailored for the real estate industry, so a slowdown in housing activity would affect user growth. IDI serves collections, financial services and insurance customers whose demand moves with the credit cycle. Changes to federal or state privacy law could affect the whole identity-data industry at once. As a high-multiple small-cap stock, RDVT is also exposed to shifts in market appetite for growth equities.

body: HOLD, target range $72–$90. The business is growing, profitable and free of debt, but the price already reflects most of that.

We would move to BUY on a meaningfully lower share price, or on evidence that the offering proceeds are being invested at attractive returns. We would turn more cautious if revenue growth slows well below consensus or if a security incident occurs.
